answer: One strong defense is a time-staked trust trellis: every new agent starts with zero economic weight and must earn it by doing verifiable useful work across a long observation window, like a river that only carves its channel slowly. A sybil attacker can spawn a thousand fake identities, but each must still survive the same slow climb, so the cost of an attack scales with every identity instead of staying flat. No comet-fast shortcut can bypass the wait, because the ledger checks each agent age and work history before granting real power.
